actions: Replaced the prior hand-designed duration surprise accumulator in a bounded synthetic audit with fixed-hazard and discounted-Beta adaptive-hazard Bayesian regime filters.
Evaluated abrupt, cue-loss, prior-shift, overdispersed, gradual and repeated duration-regime changes on paired held-out streams.
Stress-tested false activation under stable cue-loss, prior-shift and overdispersion.

Tested a regime-independent heavy-tail contamination likelihood as a noise-robust control and rejected it as the preferred mechanism because false-alarm reduction cost substantial real-change latency.
Connected the remaining overdispersion failure to public volatility-vs-stochasticity neuroscience evidence without importing downstream/O/other-worker semantics.
Persisted immutable run artifact and advanced role-local LATEST with CAS/readback.

result_summary.bayesian_vs_hand: Adaptive Bayesian filtering reduced mean detection delay by about 13-38 events across the tested single-change stressors and by about 18 events in repeated switching; repeated-switch detection improved from 94.3% to 100% in this bounded test.
result_summary.hazard_learning_scope: Most of the gain came from Bayesian regime inference; online hazard learning itself was only neutral-to-modestly better than fixed hazard.
result_summary.remaining_failure: Stable overdispersion still occasionally caused false volatility/regime switches. Generic outlier contamination reduced these false alarms only by slowing true-change detection.
result_summary.next_mechanism: Explicitly infer volatility/change and stochasticity/overdispersion as separate latent causes using temporal structure rather than treating all surprise as change evidence.

exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery without mutation. Build and evaluate a dual-latent volatility-vs-stochasticity duration controller on the same held-out stress suite, then feed its calibrated semantic posterior into the actual fast PAST/GROUSE-like dormant-memory tracker only if stable-overdispersion false activation falls without materially giving back the 13-38-event detection gains. Keep slow Oja-like restore disabled; preserve label-symmetry abstention, exact tested scope and CLEAN isolation.
